kurz: Why exchange rates almost never match the value that theory calculates, and how they affect a portfolio.

bloecke.md:
An exchange rate is a price like any other, except that there is money on both sides. In Europe, exchange rates are expressed as an [[indirect quotation]]. EUR/USD 1.10 means that one euro costs $1.10. If this number rises, the euro appreciates and the dollar depreciates. For a portfolio with dollar investments, that is the unfavourable direction. The inverse ratio (€0.91 per dollar) gives the same information as a direct quotation. This is where much of the confusion about exchange rates arises.

The foreign exchange market is the largest financial market in the world. The triennial survey of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) from April 2025 measures daily turnover of $9.5 trillion, 27% more than in 2022. Only a small part of this is used to pay for goods. The rest is accounted for by hedging, positioning and interdealer trading. Exchange rates can therefore be explained primarily by capital flows and expectations, and only secondarily by export statistics.

## Models for the exchange rate

[[Purchasing power parity]] is based on the law of one price. According to this law, a tradable good converted into the same currency should cost the same everywhere, because otherwise arbitrage would pay off. In this absolute version, purchasing power parity has been refuted empirically, because price levels differ persistently and considerably. This is not a market failure. Rents, haircuts and restaurant meals are not traded across borders and are systematically cheaper in economies with lower productivity (Balassa-Samuelson effect). A currency is therefore not undervalued merely because the price level in the country is low.

The relative version is useful. According to it, the currency with the higher inflation tends to depreciate over long periods. As a forecast for a quarter it is worthless, but as a guide over ten or twenty years it proves its worth.

bloecke.formel: Change in EUR/USD (% p.a.) ~ US inflation - euro area inflation
bloecke.erklaerung: The formula describes relative purchasing power parity using indirect quotation. Higher inflation in the US points to a rising euro exchange rate, that is to a weaker dollar.
bloecke.beispiel: As of August 2026: US inflation 3.4%, euro area 3.0% for 2026 according to the ECB projection. The difference of 0.4 percentage points cannot be seen in the daily fluctuations, but over twenty years it adds up to a difference of around 8%.

bloecke.md: The second model works with interest rates instead of prices. [[Covered interest parity]] is an arbitrage condition and does not depend on expectations. An investor can exchange euros for dollars today, invest the money short term in the US and immediately lock in the exchange back into euros with a forward contract. In this way, the investor cannot earn more than with a euro investment, as otherwise there would be a risk-free profit. The interest rate differential is therefore contained in the forward rate. It is part of the price and not an advantage for the investor. Since the financial crisis there have been measurable deviations, because bank balance sheet capacity is scarce and regulated. This does not change the order of magnitude.

bloecke.formel: Forward rate (USD per EUR) = Spot rate × (1 + i_USD) / (1 + i_EUR)
bloecke.erklaerung: The forward rate fully reflects the interest rate differential. The factor formed from the two interest rates is thus the ongoing price of currency hedging.
bloecke.beispiel: As of September 2026: Fed target range 3.75% to 4.00% (midpoint 3.875%), ECB deposit facility rate 2.50%. 1.03875 / 1.025 = 1.0134. On a twelve-month horizon, the dollar is therefore quoted around 1.3% weaker on the forward market than on the spot market. Investors who hedge dollar investments into euros pay approximately this 1.3% a year.

bloecke.titel: Interest rates and inflation in the euro area and the US, September 2026
bloecke.unter: The difference in short-term interest rates determines the price of hedging; the difference in long-term yields is one reason for capital inflows into dollar investments.

bloecke.md:
The ECB's deposit facility rate has been 2.50% since 16 September 2026, and the Fed target range has been 3.75% to 4.00% since 17 September. Ten-year German federal bonds (Bunds) yielded around 3.5% in mid-September, and ten-year US government bonds (Treasuries) 4.94% on 17 September. **Uncovered interest parity** states that this interest rate advantage is offset, in expectation, by a depreciation of the dollar. Empirically, this is regarded as the best-known failed prediction in macroeconomics, because high-interest currencies have on historical average tended to appreciate rather than depreciate.

The [[carry trade]] is based on this deviation. It involves borrowing in a low-interest currency and investing the money in a high-interest currency. The return is the interest rate differential, as long as the exchange rate remains stable. It is well documented that the strategy was profitable on average over long periods. Equally well documented is the distribution of outcomes, with many small gains and rare, very large losses. The premium is compensation for the risk of a sudden crash. On 5 August 2024 the Nikkei 225 lost around 12% in a single day after the Bank of Japan had raised interest rates and the yen had surged. The crash was triggered by the simultaneous buying back of borrowed yen and not by the state of the Japanese economy. The record turnover in the BIS survey dates from April 2025, a month in which the dollar depreciated sharply after 2 April.

bloecke.titel: High interest rates in foreign currency
bloecke.md: An instant-access savings account in a high-interest currency paying 8% interest only appears to be above the German interest rate level. This offer contains an expected depreciation of several per cent, and the forward market shows this price openly. Investors who want to collect the interest rate advantage have to bear the currency risk unhedged. With hedging, practically nothing of the difference is left after costs.

## Effects of appreciation and depreciation

A weaker euro makes European exports cheaper and all imports more expensive. Energy and many commodities are invoiced in dollars. If the oil price in dollars stays unchanged, it rises in euros when the euro falls. The German inflation rate in August 2026 was 2.9% compared with the previous year. It was driven by energy at 10.5% and fuels at 27.7%, while the core rate excluding food and energy stayed at 2.4%. The exchange rate always plays a part in price developments like these.

This is why the exchange rate is also a transmission channel of monetary policy. Higher interest rates attract capital, the currency appreciates, imports become cheaper and inflation falls. The ECB explicitly counts the exchange rate channel among its transmission channels, with the usual caveat that the effect comes through with long and uncertain lags.

bloecke.md:
## The dollar as the leading currency

The dollar's position as the leading currency rests on a self-reinforcing network effect and not on any demand by the United States. Market participants who invoice in dollars are paid in dollars. They hold dollar reserves, borrow in dollars and find the deepest markets for the dollar. At the end of 2025, around 57% of official foreign exchange reserves were held in dollars and around 20% in euros. In SWIFT payment messages the dollar accounted for around 48% in 2025, the euro for 23% and the renminbi for 4%. In foreign exchange trading, the dollar is on one side of almost 90% of all transactions.

bloecke.titel: Shares of the dollar and the euro by use
bloecke.unter: In foreign exchange trading, all shares add up to 200%, because two currencies are involved in every transaction. The renminbi reaches 9% there and 4% in SWIFT messages.
kategorien: Official foreign exchange reserves, end of 2025

bloecke.md: Gold's share of total official reserves rose to 27% at the end of 2025, putting it above the euro's share of 15%. This looks like a turn away from the dollar. Calculated at end-2023 prices, however, the same gold holdings would come to 16%. The increase is therefore largely a valuation effect, because the gold price rose by around 27% in 2024 and by around 65% in 2025. In addition, in mid-2025 fewer than 10% of reserve managers cited US tariffs as a reason for their allocation, and according to market analyses China continued to buy dollars. Reserves are therefore becoming more widely spread, but there is no sign of the dollar being replaced. It also remains open whether a currency without a common fiscal policy can become the successor to a world currency at all.

## A currency area without an internal exchange rate

Among its members, the euro has abolished the exchange rate as an adjustment tool. If a country loses competitiveness, it cannot devalue. What remains is [[internal devaluation]] through falling wages, prices and employment, which is slower, more visible and politically more costly than a devaluation of the currency. Every debate about the euro revolves around this construction: one monetary policy and twenty-one fiscal policies, with no exchange rate to balance things out between them.

This becomes visible in the balances of the payment system, which has been called T2 since March 2023. If an Italian customer transfers money to a German account, the Bundesbank acquires a claim on the Eurosystem and the Banca d'Italia a liability. At its peak, the German claim reached the order of one trillion euros. According to one reading, these balances are merely an accounting item that arises automatically anyway when central banks buy bonds. According to the other, they are an accumulated risk that would turn into a real loss if a country left. Both readings are correct within their respective frameworks, and the dispute has not been settled. Accounts that present it as settled are pursuing an agenda of their own.

## Exchange rate risk in the portfolio

A portfolio of global equities is invested largely in dollars. The US share of global equity indices has been around 70% for years. In addition, there are companies that are listed outside the US but report in dollars. Price return and currency movement are multiplied together and not added.

An ETF on a world index that is traded on the stock exchange in euros and settled in euros carries the same currency risk as the same fund in dollars. The risk lies in the companies and their revenues and not in the trading currency. Only an explicitly currency-hedged share class (usually with the suffix *EUR hedged*) changes this. In return, it costs the interest rate differential on an ongoing basis.

bloecke.titel: One year of a dollar investment, calculated in euros

bloecke.md:
The calculation is multiplicative: 1.08 × 0.90 = 0.972, that is minus 2.8%. An 8% gain in the investment currency can turn into a loss in euros.

Whether hedging is worthwhile depends on the asset class. With bonds, currency fluctuation is regularly a multiple of the expected yield differential. An unhedged foreign currency bond is therefore mainly a bet on the exchange rate, with an interest coupon on top. Investors who hold bonds to stabilise their portfolio should therefore hold them in euros or hedge them. With equities, the situation is less clear-cut. Hedging costs the interest rate differential on an ongoing basis, currently around 1.3% a year against the dollar. In addition, the dollar often appreciates in crises and so cushions losses for euro investors precisely when prices are falling. Holding a globally diversified equity portfolio unhedged is therefore a defensible decision. It should, however, be made deliberately and after careful consideration.

In a portfolio, currency risk is rarely dangerous. It becomes dangerous on the balance sheet when income arises in one currency and debts in another. The Asian financial crisis began on 2 July 1997, when Thailand abandoned the baht's peg to the dollar. The exchange rate immediately collapsed by 15% to 20%, and banks with dollar debts and baht claims became insolvent. In 1998 Indonesia's gross domestic product shrank by 13.1%. For private individuals, the equivalent is a foreign currency loan, for example financing in Swiss francs with income in euros.

An interest rate advantage that is visible on the forward market is a price and not a return. An interest rate advantage that can only be collected unhedged is a risk premium. For this premium, the investor bears a risk of loss that will materialise at some point.

Loans have been taken out in dollars all over the world, including by debtors without dollar income. When funding becomes scarce, these debtors have to buy dollars, regardless of the trigger and even when the crisis, as it often does, originates in the United States. At the same time, US government bonds are the deepest and most liquid market, into which large investors can retreat in phases of panic. Both drive the dollar exchange rate up while share prices fall. This relationship cushions the impact of crises on a euro portfolio, but it is not guaranteed. In April 2025 the dollar fell while the markets were under pressure.

mitnehmen: The forward rate fully reflects the interest rate differential, so a visible interest rate advantage in a foreign currency is never free.
Purchasing power parity works over decades, interest rates and expectations work over months, and there is no useful exchange rate forecast for short periods.
Price return and exchange rate are multiplied, so that plus 8% in dollars becomes minus 2.8% in euros if the dollar depreciates by 10%.
The trading currency of an ETF says nothing about its currency risk; what matters is where the revenues of the companies it holds come from.
The dollar is losing some of its unique position but remains dominant, and the much-discussed rise in gold's share of reserves is mainly a price effect.

begriffe.text: Statement of how many units of foreign currency one unit of the domestic currency costs. EUR/USD 1.10 means that one euro costs $1.10. If the number rises, the euro appreciates.

Assumption that identical goods cost the same everywhere once converted into the same currency. In its absolute version it does not hold. The relative version explains long-term exchange rate trends by differences in inflation.
Arbitrage condition under which the forward rate between two currencies fully reflects their interest rate differential. It determines the ongoing cost of currency hedging.

Strategy in which an investor borrows in a low-interest currency and invests the money in a high-interest currency. Historically it has been profitable on average, but it produces rare, very large losses when the positions are unwound.
Restoring competitiveness through falling wages, prices and employment when no exchange rate of one's own is available. Within a monetary union it serves as a substitute for a devaluation.
